Specify an event rate model

Source: R/event_rate.R
specify_event_rate.Rd

specify_event_rate() brings an event rate panel (from build_event_panel()) and optional fixed device covariates into infer's native specify(), declaring the model formula for the event counts and setting log(exposure)—with exposure expressed in the panel's exposure_unit—as the model offset. Passing the result to fit() fits a Poisson rate model via stats::glm(); devices with positive exposure and zero events remain in the model.

Usage

specify_event_rate(panel, formula, covariates = NULL)

Arguments

panel

An event_panel object, the output of build_event_panel().

formula

A model formula with the panel's events column on the left-hand side and device covariates on the right-hand side, e.g. events ~ region. Use events ~ 1 for an intercept-only (overall rate) model.

covariates

An optional data frame of fixed device covariates, with exactly one row per device and the same device column as the inputs to build_event_panel(). Every device with effective exposure must be present.

Value

An infer object (see specify()) carrying an offset attribute; pass it to fit() to fit the Poisson rate model.

See also

Other event rate functions: build_event_panel(), fit_event_rate()

Examples

online <- data.frame(
  device = c("a", "a", "b"),
  start = c(0, 5, 0),
  end = c(10, 15, 8)
)
events <- data.frame(
  device = c("a", "a", "b"),
  event_id = c("e1", "e1", "e2"),
  time = c(3, 3, 7)
)
covariates <- data.frame(
  device = c("a", "b"),
  region = c("north", "south")
)

panel <- build_event_panel(online, events, period = c(0, 20))
specify_event_rate(panel, events ~ region, covariates = covariates)
#> Response: events (numeric)
#> Explanatory: region (factor)
#> Offset: log_...
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   events region log_exposure
#>    <dbl> <fct>         <dbl>
#> 1      1 north          2.71
#> 2      1 south          2.08
